keys: `with.paginate` (a map) makes a `run: api` step repeat its request and collect one list. `strategy`: `cursor` (default) or `page`. `items_field`: where the list is in each JSON answer, a dotted path (`$.data`, `$.result.rows`, or `$` when the answer itself is the list; default `$.items`; no `[0]` indexing). `max_pages`: a whole number from 1 to 500 (default 50). cursor: `cursor_field`, the dotted path of the next cursor in each answer, is required; `cursor_param` is the query parameter the cursor goes out in (default `cursor`). page: `page_param` (default `page`) and `page_start` (the first page number, 0 or higher; default 1, and 0 for an upstream that numbers its pages from 0). Write `max_pages` and `page_start` as plain numbers, not quoted text, and the paths as literal text (no `${{ }}`). A block that is not a map, any other key, a key of the other strategy and a value outside these are refused when the file is written (checked_values → paginate).
requests: Every page is the step's own request (method, headers, auth, `sign:`, `query:`, body) plus that one query parameter; `timeout:` applies to each page and `success_when:` is tested on each. cursor: the first request carries no cursor, each later one the cursor from the answer before, and it ends when an answer has no items or no cursor. page: the number goes up by one until an answer has no items, so an upstream that ignores the parameter is read `max_pages` times. Both end at `max_pages` without an error.
outputs: They replace the single-call outputs: `steps.<id>.outputs.items` (the items of every page, in order), `item_count`, `pages_fetched` (answers received, an empty last page included) and `last_status`. The step needs an `id:`. A page that fails (an error status, a timeout, an answer over 1 MiB, `success_when` false) fails the step. `handled_statuses` cannot be combined with `paginate` (refused when written), and a step-level `retry:` starts again from the first page.
check: The loop ends quietly, so assert what you expected: `pages_fetched` equal to `max_pages` means there may be more, and `item_count` 0 where rows were expected usually means `items_field` names nothing, or an object rather than a list. A `for_each` over `items` takes at most 10,000 elements (loop_sources). An unknown `strategy` and a cursor strategy with no `cursor_field` are refused when the file is written; in an app that already has one the step fails when it runs, before it sends a request (`paginate: unknown strategy "offset" (use 'cursor' or 'page')`).
yaml_example:
# flows/sync-contacts.yaml - read every page of an upstream list, then store the rows
on:
  request:
    method: POST
    path: /api/contacts/sync
    role: admin
    mode: async                    # many pages can outlast a synchronous flow's time limit
jobs:
  sync:
    steps:
      - id: list
        run: api
        with:
          url: https://api.example.com/v1/contacts
          headers: { Authorization: "Bearer ${{ env.CRM_TOKEN }}" }
          query: { limit: "100" }  # sent with every page
          paginate:
            strategy: cursor       # or: page
            cursor_field: $.next   # where each answer carries the next cursor
            cursor_param: after    # sent as ?after=<cursor> from the second page on
            items_field: $.data    # the list inside each answer
            max_pages: 20
      - for_each: ${{ steps.list.outputs.items }}
        as: c
        steps:
          - run: sql
            with:
              query: "INSERT INTO contacts (external_id, name, email) VALUES (:ext, :name, :email) ON CONFLICT (external_id) DO UPDATE SET name = excluded.name, email = excluded.email"
              params: { ext: "${{ c.id }}", name: "${{ c.name }}", email: "${{ c.email || '' }}" }
      - run: sql
        with:
          query: "INSERT INTO maintenance_runs (kind, changed) VALUES ('sync-contacts', :changed)"
          params: { changed: "${{ steps.list.outputs.item_count }}" }
